articles.title: Warp Sciences Emerges From Stealth With $215M for AI-Powered Chemistry Labs
articles.snippet: Warp Sciences Emerges From Stealth With $215M for AI-Powered Chemistry Labs Unite.AI
articles.text:

Warp Sciences Emerges From Stealth With $215M for AI-Powered Chemistry Labs
Published
October 22, 2026
By
Evan Mercer, AI Startups & Venture Capital AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Co-Founders: Kevin Weil (CEO), DJ Patil (COO), Sol Reisberg (Chief Scientific Officer), and Mano Paluri (CTO).
Designing a promising molecule is only the beginning of drug research. Someone still has to make it, test it, and turn the results into a better next experiment. Warp Sciences is betting that this physical bottleneck is where AI can create its next major advantage.
Warp Sciences has emerged from stealth with $215 million in funding to build a U.S.-based chemistry contract research organization, or CRO, combining experienced chemists, AI, and robotics. Led by former OpenAI Chief Product Officer Kevin Weil, the company plans to provide research compounds to biotech and pharmaceutical customers while building laboratories that learn from the experiments they perform.
Lightspeed led the financing, with participation from IVP , Mayfield , Lux , Premji Invest , and Menlo Ventures , among others. Angel investors include Brian Armstrong, Mike Krieger, Dylan Field, and OpenAI’s Mark Chen and Sarah Friar.
A Chemistry Services Business Built Around AI
Warp’s starting point is lead optimization analog synthesis: making variations of molecules so researchers can compare them as they work toward a drug candidate. It is a concrete service with a deliverable, rather than a promise that an AI model will independently invent a medicine.
According to its customer services page , Warp is focused on preclinical small-molecule programs, producing compounds at milligram to multi-gram scale. The company describes its typical work as elaborated molecules requiring five to 15 synthetic steps. That scope places it inside the repeated cycle of making and evaluating compounds that research teams need to refine a program.
Warp also makes a clear distinction about ownership of the research agenda. Customers choose which molecules to pursue and retain control of their drug programs. Warp has no proprietary drug pipeline of its own. Its business is supplying the chemistry and experimental infrastructure those teams use.
That matters commercially. A CRO has to deliver usable compounds, maintain quality, and collaborate effectively with customer scientists. Those requirements give Warp’s automation effort an immediate operational test: whether it makes the service more productive and dependable.
From Laboratory Results to Better Models
The longer-term technology thesis is a feedback loop between experimentation and machine learning. Physical experiments produce evidence about what works. AI systems learn from that evidence, help guide subsequent experiments, and support increasingly automated laboratory work. More capable labs can then produce more useful evidence.
In its founders’ manifesto , Warp says it plans to capture both successful experiments and failures. Alongside customer work, it intends to run dedicated experimental campaigns to generate data for its models. Experienced chemists will lead the laboratories as more of the workflow is automated.

articles.text:
Ledgebrook raises USD 200 million in primary equity financing co-led by Allianz X to scale AI-native specialty insurance platform
News provided by
Ledgebrook
Oct 07, 2026, 08:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Funds will scale Ledgebrook's tech-led approach to U.S. specialty underwriting, covering custom and complex insurance needs
Ledgebrook on track to surpass USD 1 billion in cumulative premium written since it started writing business in 2023
Investment expands Allianz X's U.S. property and casualty (P&C) platform into mid-sized general liability risks in excess and surplus (E&S) market
Allianz Re agrees to enter a multi-year reinsurance agreement with Ledgebrook
BOSTON and MUNICH , Oct. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ledgebrook, the AI-native specialty insurance platform, today announced it has raised USD 200 million in primary equity financing co-led by Allianz X, the strategic investment arm of the Allianz Group, and Rockefeller Capital Management. Existing and new investors also participated. Ledgebrook will use the funds to scale its technology and extend Blackbird, Ledgebrook's proprietary AI-native underwriting platform. Separately, Allianz Re has agreed to enter a multi-year reinsurance agreement with Ledgebrook.
Continue Reading
Gage Caligaris, founder and CEO, Ledgebrook and Dr. Nazim Cetin, CEO, Alllianz X
Headquartered in Boston, Ledgebrook sits between the brokers who need cover for hard-to-place risks and the capital that backs them, running on technology it built from the ground up. It writes general liability, professional liability, and specialty cover for mid-sized-market businesses in the E&S market, distributed exclusively through wholesale brokers. Ledgebrook's proprietary AI-based platform, Blackbird, reads submissions, classifies risk, and calculates a technical price, quoting specialty risks, often in hours rather than weeks, with experienced underwriters making the final decision. As such, brokers, and therefore their clients, get fast, reliable answers on placing risks. Ledgebrook's approach has put it on track to surpass USD 1 billion in cumulative premium written since it started writing business in 2023.
Gage Caligaris, Founder & CEO of Ledgebrook, said : "Our vision is for Ledgebrook to be the company that makes the wheels of insurance spin faster. Businesses with complex risk deserve specialized underwriting, rated with rigor and delivered at speed. Our platform lets our underwriters do that with real discipline. Allianz X backing gives us the capital to keep investing in technology and talent. We're building this company for the long term."
Dr. Nazim Cetin, CEO of Allianz X, said: "The industry is applying AI to its simplest risks first, because that is where automation comes easily. We think the larger prize sits at the other end, in complex, hard to place business, where underwriting judgment is scarce and slow decisions cost the most. That's exactly the gap Blackbird is built to close, and it's why Ledgebrook fills a meaningful space in our U.S. P&C platform."
John Mullen, President of E&S at Ledgebrook, added : "E&S is seeing strong multi-year growth. Admitted carriers tightened their appetite and pushed risks that were once routinely placed in the admitted market into this channel, and we're excited about accelerating the delivery of value to our distribution partners and insured customers in this segment."

articles.title: Warhound raises $200M to engineer war dogs and arm them with Anduril gear
articles.snippet: Warhound raises $200M to engineer war dogs and arm them with Anduril gear TechCrunch
articles.text:
Colossal Biosciences’ Ben Lamm and Anduril’s Palmer Luckey had an idea to genetically engineer war dogs for the U.S. military, law enforcement, and other emergency response teams. On Thursday, that idea came out of stealth as Warhound , backed by $200 million in funding from investors including Sequoia, 8VC, Corner Ventures, and In-Q-Tel, a venture firm backed by the CIA and other U.S. intelligence agencies. The round values the company at $1.2 billion.
Warhound’s dogs, which do not exist yet, will take on tasks that are dangerous for humans or difficult for machines, such as bomb detection, searches, and other specialized operations. In its launch announcement, the company said that more than 80% of the U.S. military’s working dogs come from Europe, and less than half of them are fit for service.
That means the supply of working dogs is dwindling, and the U.S. increasingly relies on foreign nations for dogs that play an important role in the military and in law enforcement. Warhound aims to change that. The hope is that Colossal can use its technology to engineer dogs with “characteristics suited to demanding missions,” the company said in a press release.
Lamm told TechCrunch he met Luckey about a year ago at a conference, where Luckey said more should be done for the military’s working dogs. The two kept in touch, and Lamm researched how working dogs are bred. He learned that many of them do not make it through training because of inherited predispositions to problems like poor eyesight or the high possibilities of cancer, hip dysplasia, or muscle atrophy.
Lamm believed dogs could be enhanced for health, longevity, and “for things like speed and agility or enhance olfactory sensors for bomb sniffing and whatnot,” he said. His team studied top-performing working dog breeds — the Belgian Malinois and German Shepherd — taking cell lines (living cells grown in a lab) from them and putting them in a biobank. From there, the team will edit the dogs’ genes, adding ones that will improve performance and removing ones that will not, to create “a new type of dog.”
Anduril, meanwhile, will provide software and hardware, such as protection vests and goggles, to assist the dogs and their handlers with situational awareness and coordination. Lamm said to imagine, for example, bulletproof vests with data sensors that send information back to the handlers so they can better understand what is happening.
“The idea is, if we make the dog safer, make it healthier, make it perform better, it’s going to perform better in the line of duty,” Lamm said. He added that Anduril’s additions will make the dogs safer and healthier beyond their genetics, “on top of the dog, not in the dog.” He believes the enhancements will also better protect the dogs’ human handlers.
Luckey is a partner in the venture but owns no equity in it, Lamm told TechCrunch. Colossal owns equity in the business and supports it by licensing its technology.
Colossal is currently known for its de-extinction efforts to bring back animals like the dodo and the mammoth . As Lamm previously told TechCrunch, the company has been using AI, buying and building technology to help with gene cloning and with identifying and copying animal genes.

articles.text:
© Liviorki for Evertiq
General | October 05, 2026
SiMa.ai raises $150 million in Series C to scale Physical AI
Evertiq
The new funding brings the total capital raised by the US startup to USD 500 million, valuing it at USD 1.45 billion. The fresh capital will accelerate the scaling of Palette Neat, an agentic software environment for Physical AI.
SiMa.ai has announced USD 150 million in Series C financing, bringing the total capital raised to USD 500 million and valuing the San Jose, California-based startup at USD 1.45 billion.
The round was co-led by Fidelity Management & Research Company and Amplify, with participation from Alter Venture Partners, Dell Technologies Capital, Maverick Capital, +ND Capital, Point72 and StepStone Group. AllianceBernstein, Baron Capital, J.P. Morgan, and the State of Michigan also joined the round as new investors, SiMa.ai said in a press release.
SiMa.ai delivers a full-stack Physical AI platform combining purpose-built silicon and software to streamline deployments from months to days or hours, the company said.
“Physical AI in humanoids, automotive and drones is the gateway to a $50 trillion market that has remained largely untouched by modern innovation,” said Krishna Rangasayee, Founder and CEO at SiMa.ai. “While others are still figuring out the pieces or repurposing their cloud offerings, we’ve built the entire puzzle. This investment will further catapult us into a dominant position, giving us the resources to scale our purpose-built platform and secure an undeniable lead in the Physical AI race.”
This capital raise will accelerate the scaling of Palette Neat, an agentic software environment for Physical AI, and fund next-generation hardware that will deliver 1,000 dense TOPS of compute in purpose-built Physical AI silicon, the press release said.
“SiMa.ai has consistently proven its ability to out-innovate and out-execute the rest of the market, dramatically reducing the complexity of deploying advanced AI models on physical edge devices, and accelerating time to market for the world’s most sophisticated autonomous systems,” said Mike Dauber, General Partner, Amplify Partners
“As enterprise intelligence migrates into the physical world, it’s been challenged by the tradeoff between performance and power. SiMa.ai is shattering that barrier,” said Scott Darling, President and Managing Director, Dell Technologies Capital. “Its platform delivers the software agility and Physical AI-optimized compute that modern enterprises require to scale computer vision and autonomous capabilities.”
John Avirett, Partner, StepStone Group, said SiMa.ai had created a differentiated, purpose-built Physical AI platform that answers the rigorous demands of real-world applications.

articles.title: Supabase raises another $150M to build the backend for AI coding from Singapore
articles.snippet: Supabase raises another $150M to build the backend for AI coding from Singapore Asia Tech Review
articles.text:
Supabase raises another $150M to build the backend for AI coding from Singapore
New funding comes months after $500M raise and includes strategic acquisition
Jon Russell
Oct 05, 2026
7
1
Share
Welcome back to Asia Tech Review, your curated digest to keep up to date with tech news across Asia.
Supabase might just be the best example of a new tech startup in Singapore. It has built a fast-growing and global business that’s been backed with over $1 billion from investors across the world. And it’s building core tools for the agentic era. Today, we look at its newest round, an acquisition and its future goals.
To keep up with our issues, follow us on LinkedIn or WhatsApp . Please do share Asia Tech Review with people you know who want to get smart about Asia tech.
For news as it happens, follow ATR Bulletin , our real-time news site that keeps you in the know.
The tech startup blueprint Singapore wants to see more of
Supabase, the Singapore-based database platform that helps developers build apps and software, closed a $150 million funding round , just four months after it announced a $500 million Series F round.
The round is led by GIC, the Singapore sovereign fund, and it includes Google’s CapitalG fund for the first time. That’s notable as one of the main competitors of Supabase’s developer stack is Google-owned Firebase. Still, Supabase CEO Paul Copplestone said the fund’s “connections to the broader Alphabet ecosystem will be invaluable as we build for our next level of growth.”
You don’t typically see a smaller round like this follow a huge raise like Supabase’s Series F, but in this case the startup’s recent growth spurt is such that it appears to need the funds to support continuing to accelerate its trajectory.
“Supabase is now adding more than 1M users and 4M databases per month with 70% of new databases created by agents or AI-driven tools. The growth follows a 600% year-over-year increase in databases reported in June, when agents were already deploying the majority of new databases on the platform,” the company wrote.
Supabase has raised over $1 billion in total from investors that include Accel, Peak XV, Craft, Coatue, Y Combinator, Stripe, Salesforce Ventures and Figma.
It’s worth recalling what Supabase does. It provides a set of backend tools to enable developers to quickly build and develop apps, websites and other software using a central resource to manage files, authentication, databases and more. In the agentic era which allows software to be created in minutes or hours not days, that’s a particularly key tech stack as Supabase’s numbers seem to show.
That explains why, alongside the funding round, it announced that it acquired a startup called Turso , which allows databases to be provisioned on demand. That makes perfect sense for Supabase since vibe- and agentic-coding is sending its numbers skyrocketing, it needs the tools to support faster creation of databases and the plumbing beyond apps, websites and more.
Whether you create a web app for friends, a private CRM tool for your company or a new product for an existing customer base, Supabase wants to make its tools the go to for Claude, ChatGPT or bots like Muse, Grok Bot or Dots.
